author: Inside Edition
description: Angela Perryman is on quarantine lockdown after being a passenger on the cruise ship hit with the Hantavirus. Perryman says she is being held against her will at the National Quarantine Unit in Nebraska. The National Quarantine Unit has allowed 8 of the 18 Americans who were on the ship to voluntarily finish quarantine at home under strict 24 hour surveillance. Perryman wants to go back to Florida but the state does not agree with the federal government requirement for surveillance. Perryman has not tested positive or shown symptoms of the Hantavirus and understands the need to quarantine.
title: Woman Says She's Living A Nightmare In Quarantine Lockdown After Being On Hantavirus-Hit Cruise Ship

author: Inside Edition
description: Jhoen Lefont is a world class talent at bouncing a ball on his head while treading water. The Cuban swimmer-bouncer just broke his own world records for the most touches in one minute and most touches in 30 seconds while in the water. Judges were on hand to time him and count the bounces. When it became clear he'd broken his own 2025 Guinness World Records, there were cheers and hugs with his supporters on 'Team Lefont' at a pool in Havana.
title: Cuban Athlete Breaks Own Record For Aquatic Ball Control

author: Inside Edition
description: Bodycam video shows intense moments on a Missouri Highway as a suspect shoots at a trooper's vehicle. The Missouri State Highway Patrol released this video of the incident. It says several law enforcement agencies were pursuing the vehicle, which was being driven by a homicide suspect. A trooper drove up to the vehicle and performed a PIT maneuver. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Suspect Shoots Through Trooper's Window During High-Speed Chase

author: Inside Edition
description: A terrifying moment was caught on camera, as a Jollibee fast food restaurant collapsed during a recent earthquake in the Philippines. It was located in General Santos, the region worst hit by the natural disaster. The 7.8-magnitude earthquake hit early Monday morning. Experts say it was one of the strongest quakes to hit the country in 50 years. Dozens of people have been reported dead, over 400 have been injured, and several are still missing.
title: Jollibee Fast-Food Restaurant Flattened During Philippines Earthquake
